title: FEAST: Federated Shared-Space Training for Resource-Heterogeneous Clients
abstract: arXiv:2608.09250v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Federated learning (FL) must serve devices with varying computational capabilities. A fixed model cannot suit all devices, while training one model per deployment limit is costly. Federated supernet training instead learns one elastic model with differently sized subnetworks, then deploys a suitable one to each device. When client inference budgets differ, however, parameters exclusive to high-cost subnetworks are reachable by fewer clients. We propose FEAST, a federated shared-space training framework that counters this imbalance by jointly training multiple subnetworks within each client's limit. Budget-tailored sub-supernet routing sends only the relevant supernet portion, and sparse aggregation merges the returned parameter slices. The trained supernet directly serves the subnetworks used during federation and supports post-hoc extraction of additional subnetworks without federated retraining. translated_title: FEAST：面向资源异构客户端的联邦共享空间训练
translated_abstract: 联邦学习（FL）必须服务于具有不同计算能力的设备。固定模型无法适配所有设备，而针对每种部署限制单独训练一个模型的成本又很高。联邦超网训练转而学习一个包含不同大小子网络的弹性模型，然后为每个设备部署合适的子网络。然而，当客户端的推理预算各不相同时，高成本子网络独有的参数只能被较少的客户端访问到。我们提出了FEAST，一个联邦共享空间训练框架，通过在每个客户端的资源限制内联合训练多个子网络来对抗这种不平衡。预算定制的子超网路由只发送相关的超网部分，稀疏聚合则合并返回的参数切片。训练得到的超网可直接服务于联邦训练期间使用的子网络，并支持在不进行联邦重训的情况下事后提取额外的子网络。我们进一步表明，独立……
tldr: FEAST通过在每个客户端资源预算内联合训练多个子网络，并结合预算定制的子超网路由与稀疏聚合机制，解决了联邦学习中因客户端资源异构导致的参数训练不平衡问题，且支持无需联邦重训即可事后提取新子网络。
en_tdlr: FEAST is a federated shared-space training framework that tackles the imbalance caused by resource-heterogeneous clients by jointly training multiple subnetworks within each client's budget, using budget-tailored sub-supernet routing and sparse aggregation, while enabling post-hoc extraction of additional subnetworks without federated retraining.
